title: Factor Analysis with Correlated Topic Model for Multi-Modal Data
venue: Proceedings of the 28th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2025), PMLR 258
subcategory: Bayesian factor analysis joined with correlated topic model
task: Integrating simple (vector) views with structured views such as text
problem: Multimodal factor analysis cannot handle structured views (text, single-cell data) where each sample has many clustered data points.
architecture: FACTM: multi-view Bayesian factor analysis with sparsity priors linked to a correlated topic model on structured views through sample-specific shifts of topic proportions; variational inference; supervised rotation of factors for interpretability.

datasets.name: CMU-MOSI
datasets.details: opinion video clips; transcripts as structured view

datasets.name: Mirex
datasets.details: songs with acoustic, melody and text features; lyrics as structured view; 5 mood classes

datasets.name: COVID-19
datasets.details: long-COVID patient data (flow cytometry, CT scans and other modalities)

key_results: Topic-based representations (ROC-AUC): Mirex 0.64 vs CTM 0.57 and LDA 0.62; Mosi 0.61 vs 0.57; but Mosei 0.63 vs LDA 0.66.
Factor-based representations differ little across models (e.g. Mosei 0.73 for FACTM, FA+CTM and MOFA).
strengths: Brings correlated topic modelling into multimodal factor analysis with an estimated topic covariance.

limitations.text: Linear dependencies and conjugacy assumptions limit expressiveness; hyperparameters fixed rather than learned.
Gains on benchmarks are small or mixed (LDA is better on Mosei).

notes: Key uses the first author's surname (Łazęcka).
